chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Musāfir, and from Al-Washshāʾ, from Musāfir, who said:

When Hārūn ibn Al-Musayyab intended to confront Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, Abū Al-Ḥasan Al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to me: “Go to him and say to him: Do not go out tomorrow, for if you go out tomorrow you will be defeated and your companions will be killed. If he asks you from where you came to know this, then say: I saw it in a dream.”

He said: So I went to him and said to him: “May I be made your ransom, do not go out tomorrow, for if you go out you will be defeated and your companions will be killed.” So he said to me: “From where did you come to know this?” I said: “I saw it in a dream.” So he said: “The servant sleeps and has not washed his behind.” Then he went out, and he was defeated, and his companions were killed.

He said: And Musāfir narrated to me, saying: I was with Abū Al-Ḥasan Al-Riḍā عليه السلام at Minā, and Yaḥyā ibn Khālid passed by and covered his head from the dust. So he said: “Poor ones, they do not know what will befall them in this year.” Then he said: “Even more astonishing than this is Hārūn and I being like these two,” and he joined his two fingers together.
Musāfir said: So by Allah, I did not know the meaning of his statement until we buried him with him.

key_terms.أَصْحَابُكَ: your companions or followers accompanying you
key_terms.الْمَنَامِ: a dream, cited here as the outward explanation given for knowing a future event
key_terms.بِمِنًى: at Minā, the well-known site during hajj
key_terms.حَدِيثِهِ: his statement or report, referring to the Imam’s earlier words
key_terms.مَسَاكِينُ: poor ones; an expression of pity for those unaware of what will happen
key_terms.هُزِمْتَ: you will be defeated in battle

ai.seo_question: How does the hadith of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام describe his foreknowledge of future events?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts a foretelling by Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام concerning a military defeat and the death of companions, which occurred exactly as stated. It also relates another statement of the Imam عليه السلام indicating the nearness of his burial alongside Hārūn, highlighting his divinely granted knowledge of unfolding events.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Musafir, and from Al Washha, from Musafir who said,

‘When Al-Haroun Ibn Al-Musayyab intended to fight Muhammad Bin Ja’far, Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Go to him and say to him, ‘Do not go out tomorrow, for you, if you do go out tomorrow, would be overcome and your companions would be killed’. So if he asks you from where you have come to know this, so say, ‘I saw it in the dream’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So I went over to him and said to him, ‘May I be sacrificed for you! Do not go out tomorrow, for if you do go out, you would be overcome and your companions would be killed’. So he said to me, ‘From where did you come to know this?’ So I said, ‘I saw it in the dream’. So he said, ‘The slave sleeps and does not (even) wash his behind?’ Then he did go out, and he was overcome and his companions were killed’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Musafir narrated to me saying, ‘I was with Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> at Mina, and Yahya Bin Khalid passed by, and he had covered his head from the dust. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The poor are not knowing what would be happening with then during this year’. Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And even more strange than this is that Haroun and I<sup>asws</sup> would be like this’, and he<sup>asws</sup> pressed his two fingers together’.
Musafir said, ‘So, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I did not know the meaning of his<sup>asws</sup> Hadeeth until he<sup>asws</sup> was buried with (near to) him’.
en.sarwar: 9. al-Husayn ibnmmd has narrated from Mu‘alla ibnmd from Musafir and from al-Washsha’ from Musafir who has said the following.

“When Harun ibn al-Musayyib decided to fight Muhammad ibn Ja‘far, abu al-Hassan (a.s.) told me to go to him and say, “Do not go our tomorrow. If would do so you will be defeated and your people will be killed.” If he would ask, “How do youknow that?” Say, “I saw it in my dream.”

The narrator has said that he went to him and said, “May Allah make of service to you, do not go out tomorrow to fight. If would do so you will be defeated and your people will be killed.” He asked, “How do you know this?” I said, “I saw it in my dream.” He said, “A slave goes to sleep (to dream) and his behind is not even washed.” He went out to fight. He was defeated and his people were killed.”

The narrator has said that Musafir narrated, “I was in the presenceof al-Rida (a.s.) in Mina, Makka that Yahya ibn Khalid passed by and he covered his head from the dust. The Imam (a.s.) said, “Poor people do not know what will happen to them this year.”
I, by Allah, could not understand themeaning of his statement until we buried him (Yahya ibn Khalid).”
